outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: In the edited image, is there clear evidence that the requested paper has begun entering or is inside the requested cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the paper and cup are identifiable and visible evidence shows some of the paper entering or inside the cup. Fail only when both objects and their relevant placement are clearly visible and the paper remains outside, with no entry. Unknown if either object or their spatial relation cannot be verified; do not infer progress or absence from a similar-looking object or from the paper being held.
nodes.binding: Assess only progress on stuffing the source paper into the source cup, using source and edited images. Verify the objects and their spatial relation in the edited image; proximity, contact with the rim, or an unverified object match is not entry.

nodes.question: Using the source image to identify the requested objects, does the edited image clearly show the paper stuffed inside the cup, rather than merely entering, resting on the rim, or being held nearby?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source paper and cup are identifiable in the edited image and the paper is visibly inside with evidence of stuffing, not merely partial entry or rim contact. Fail only if the objects and relation are clear and show that this completed condition is not met. Unknown if identity, visibility, or relation is ambiguous.
nodes.binding: Investigate the completed stuffing condition directly in the images, using s1 as context but independently inspecting the visual evidence. Do not treat s1's observation as proof of object identity or completion.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Treat s1 and s2 as one evidence chain, not independent corroboration. Complete only when s2 passes. Partial only when s1 passes and s2 fails, establishing visible entry but not completed stuffing. Absent only when s1 fails on a clear view showing no entry; s2 failure alone does not establish absence. Unknown when necessary object identity or placement evidence is unresolved, or when the observations do not support one of those states.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":true,"reason":"The program preserves the requested change: it checks whether the source paper is stuffed into the source cup, distinguishes visible entry from completed stuffing, and treats unclear identity or placement as unresolved. The nested support checks inspect their own evidence, while the fulfillment readout composes them as one evidence chain: completion requires the finer check to pass, partial requires entry plus a clear failure of completion, and absence requires a clear failure of entry. This avoids treating a coarse pass as completion or a finer failure alone as no progress. No unrelated constraints or unsupported inferences are added."}
